note: The first record in this repo, and it exists mainly to demonstrate what the schema refuses. continuous_torque_nm is null on a good datasheet from a vendor who explicitly states the distinction: 'The given Stall torque rating for a servo is different from its continuous output rating.' ROBOTIS names it, publishes a performance graph, and publishes no continuous figure. So capacity over this actuator is UNDERIVABLE and every hold answer naming it will say so — which is ADR-0004 working, not failing. Do not fill it from the 30-50%-of-stall rule of thumb; that range spans a factor of 1.67 and how_determined exists to reject it. The fix is a path somebody can walk: measure it, hold it to thermal steady state, record the method. Three voltage rows are why ADR-0014 made these fields arrays: 3.8 to 4.8 N.m is a 26% spread across this actuator's own rated range, so a derivation that picks the wrong row is wrong by that much, silently. travel is the 0-360 deg Position Control Mode range; Extended Position Control Mode is multi-turn, so continuous_rotation is deliberately not asserted here rather than guessed. gearbox.type is absent because the datasheet section read did not state the gear train type, and backlash_rad is absent meaning UNKNOWN, never zero. No part_id: OpenPartsCore has no entry for this actuator. Its electronic/sg90 entry shows what an OPC servo record does carry - identity, bus, capabilities, connector - and what it does not: no torque, no speed, no mass. That is the actuator/parts boundary of open-questions #3, tested against a real pair of records for the first time, and the split holds. Operating temperature -5 to +80 C and the 12-bit contactless absolute encoder are recorded here as prose because the schema has no field for either.
